Subject: Multi-region Dedicated ask + initial traffic profile

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. NimbusAI is evaluating a multi-region Dedicated deployment to support our inference footprint across US-East and US-West. High level:
- Baseline: 40 peak concurrent GPU slots (split ~60/40 east/west) with <100ms p50 token latency target.
- DR requirement: RTO < 15min for traffic failover; acceptable to have a cold-warm spin for non-critical batch jobs.
- We expect burst+backup traffic in West for up to 2 hours/day.

Questions for pricing:
1) Do you price per-region pools independently or is there a bundled multi-region SKU?
2) How do you handle replication: active-active hot replica vs. hot-standby vs. cold standup?
3) Any discount structure for a phased commit (Q1: 25 GPUs, Q2: add 15, Q3: remaining 0-40)?

Attaching our initial usage matrix. Can you share a strawman pricing model + SLA credit buckets?

Thanks,
Samir

Samir —

Appreciate the clear profile. Short answers up front: we support both per-region pools and a bundled multi-region commitment; replication is configurable (hot-active, hot-standby, cold DR spin-up). Pricing and credit profile depends on the topology you pick.

A few clarifying asks before we build the strawman:
- Can you confirm whether the 40 GPUs are for inference-only or include training/finetuning slots? (pricing differs)
- Is cross-region egress acceptable for failover traffic, or do you require no egress charges between regions?
- Preferred commit phasing cadence (quarterly OK?) and any internal procurement constraints (e.g., PO vs. SOW)?

Proposed next step: we’ll send three packaging options (Baseline segmented pools, Resilient replicated pools with hot-standby, and Hybrid paygo + DR spin-up) with estimated monthly costs, SLA buckets, and recommended commit ramp.

I’ve looped Aditya (pricing) and Dev (solutions) — they’ll add the technical/ops tradeoffs.

—Olga

Date: 2026-11-29T08:10:00-08:00
Subject: internal: pricing options for Nimbus — draft numbers

Team — putting draft numbers here so Olga can share the strawman. Assumptions: inference-only, A100-equivalent baseline, 730 hours/month. Traffic split 60/40 east/west.

Option A — Segmented pools (no replication)
- Per-region baseline: $1.90 / GPU-hour
- Minimum commit: 20 GPUs (east), 12 GPUs (west)
- Burst allowance: 20% for 2 hours/day at 2x cost
- SLA: 99.9% region-level; credit tier: 5% monthly credit for p99>500ms, 10% for p99>1s

Option B — Resilient (hot-standby replicate)
- Active pool + hot-standby pool in secondary region (replicated state): baseline pricing + replication surcharge 35% of committed cost
- Minimum commit: combined 40 GPUs (20 active + 20 standby)
- SLA: 99.95% with faster recovery; credit tier: 7.5% for p99>400ms, 12.5% for >900ms

Option C — Hybrid (phased commit + DR spin-up)
- Quarter 1: 25 GPUs committed (east heavy) at $1.75 / GPU-hour with 10% phased-commit discount
- Q2 add 10 GPUs; Q3 optional add 5 GPUs
- Cold DR spin-up: reserved warm images + orchestration; spin-up minutes billed at an expedited rate ($0.60/min per GPU spun)

Discounting guidance: 10% standard on annual commit, +5% for phased/quarterly signed commit, further negotiable for multi-year. For Nimbus size, recommend Option C to reduce capital exposure and add a short hot-standby window for critical endpoints.

Attachments: slo-buckets-proposal.pdf

—Aditya

On a related note, Ben — can you confirm whether we can waive cross-region egress for the first 6 months as a promo?

Subject: Proposed packaging: segmented pools + phased commit (summary)

Samir —

Thanks for the patience — attached is a concise summary of three packaging options based on your profile and our internal pricing discussion (see attachments). High level recommendations:

1) Phased Hybrid (recommended)
- Q1 commit: 25 GPUs (east:15, west:10) at $1.75 / GPU-hour
- Q2 add 10 GPUs, Q3 optional add 5 GPUs
- Phased-commit discount: additional 5% if you sign within 30 days
- Cold DR spin-up for batch jobs: $0.60 / min per GPU spun; we include 2,000 spin-up minutes in year-1 as trial credit
- Cross-region egress: waived for first 4 months (promo)
- SLA: target p99 token latency 450ms; credit tiers in attached PDF

2) Resilient (hot-standby — higher RTO profile)
- Replication surcharge +35% on committed cost; better RTO (sub-10m) and higher SLA (99.95%)

3) Segmented pools (simpler, lowest headline cost)
- Independent region pricing; no replication; recommended if you can accept longer manual failover

Next steps: I can convert Option 1 into a commercial term sheet and DocuSign if you want to move forward. We’ve included a HubSpot deal record and prepared a draft SOW.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
